newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Petronas to list twin-towers project by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Petronas to list twin-towers project by year-end.

text.p: Malaysia's national oil company Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) said it would list its Kuala Lumpur City Centre (KLCC) project by the year-end.
The KLCC project includes the 450-metre tall Petronas twin towers, the world's tallest.
"I can confirm that we are now working to apply for the listing of KLCC by the end of the year, hopefully," said Azizan Zainol Abidin, chairman of KLCC Holdings Bhd.
At 451.9 metres (1,482 feet), the towers surpass the previous height record holder, the Sears Tower in Chicago, by 10 metres (33 feet).
Petronas owns 51 percent of KLCC Holdings.

Apart from the twin towers, the KLCC complex which sits on a 40-hectare site (100 acre), will house about 20 other office blocks, retail outlets, hotels, cinemas and restaurants in a park-like setting that has been dubbed the world's biggest city-centre real estate project.
The whole project will cost at least two billion ringgit ($790 million).
